samples.scenario: An attacker leverages a compromised SIP trunk provider to initiate vishing calls spoofing the victim's credit card company number. The attacker uses RTP stream injection to insert pre-recorded urgent messages requesting the victim to verify recent transactions by providing CVV and expiration dates. Network packet captures reveal unusual RTP payload patterns and SIP REGISTER requests from unknown IPs. Call detail records show multiple short-duration calls targeting various customers. The victim is manipulated into disclosing sensitive credit card details over the call.

samples.detection_method: Monitor SIP traffic and validate caller IDs against registered IP ranges; detect unusual RTP payload signatures indicating injected audio streams; analyze call frequency and duration anomalies; correlate authentication logs with call source IPs; implement multi-factor verification for sensitive data disclosure; educate customers to never provide card details over unsolicited calls.

samples.scenario: A vishing campaign uses an international VoIP relay network to spoof the support line of a popular online payment platform. The attacker uses SIP header manipulation and RTP stream re-injection to simulate authentic hold music and agent voices. Packet captures reveal abnormal SIP OPTIONS probes and malformed SIP headers. Call detail records show calls originating from IP ranges not registered to the legitimate provider. The victim is coerced into providing their login credentials and 2FA backup codes during the call.

samples.scenario: An attacker initiates a vishing attack by spoofing the phone number of a well-known government tax agency using a malicious SIP proxy setup. The attacker contacts the victim, claiming there is an urgent tax refund issue requiring immediate bank account verification. The attacker uses SIP REGISTER hijacking to insert their proxy into the call path. Call detail records and SIP logs reveal irregular registration patterns and unexpected proxy IP addresses. The victim is manipulated into providing their bank routing number and account number verbally.

samples.scenario: A vishing attack targeting corporate employees involves the attacker spoofing the IT helpdesk number using a compromised SIP trunk. The attacker calls employees claiming that their workstation has been compromised and requests their VPN credentials for immediate remediation. SIP signaling logs show the use of an unrecognized SIP trunk with altered From headers. CDR and PBX logs indicate multiple rapid calls to various employees from the same external IP. The victim is coerced into verbally providing their VPN username and password.
